Detect and Validate Secrets Anywhere. Map Access. Revoke Fast.

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 Find leaked secrets. Validate what’s live. Map the blast radius. Revoke fast. 

Kingfisher is a fast, free, open-source secret scanner and credential response tool built in Rust. It detects leaked secrets with hundreds of built-in rules, validates which credentials are active, maps access for supported credential types, and revokes supported secrets—all in one Apache-2.0-licensed release:

 Detect → Validate → Map → Triage → Revoke 

 - scan source code, Git history, cloud storage, container images, archives, and developer platforms
 - validate which credentials are active
 - map a leaked secret's identity, permissions, and reachable resources
 - triage findings in a browser, or output as SARIF, JSON, TOON
 - send real-time alerts to Slack, Microsoft Teams, Discord, Mattermost, Google Chat, or any JSON webhook
 - revoke supported secrets

 No Git executable required. Kingfisher reads local Git history and staged changes
and clones repositories over HTTPS using native Rust libraries. The SDKs read local Git
repositories in-process. SSH remotes require an SSH client.

 Defender workflow: Follow the end-to-end defender workflow for secret detection, validation, notifications, blast-radius mapping, and revocation.

 Embed Kingfisher in Python, Node.js, or Rust

Add native secret detection, live credential validation, and explicit revocation
to your Python, JavaScript/TypeScript (Node.js), or Rust application. The same Rust
engine and rule catalog run in-process, with no CLI subprocess required.
Kingfisher is an embeddable secret scanner that also runs as a standalone CLI .

 
 
 

Choose your language and add the SDK to your existing application:

- Python: 

 Available on PyPi
 

 Import kingfisher sdk . See the Python SDK guide and
 runnable examples for scanning, validation, rule inspection,
 and explicit revocation.

- Node.js / TypeScript: 

 Available on npmjs
 

 The stable npm SDK wraps the same Rust crates with napi-rs. See the
 Node SDK guide and source/examples. It targets
 Node.js, including VS Code workspace extensions, rather than browser/WASM runtimes.
 Explore Kingfisher Workbench, a
 commented showcase with live progress, Git-history scanning and a redacted HTML
 report, or start with the runnable recipe walkthrough;
 maintainers can follow the npm trusted-publishing setup.

- Rust: 

 

 The validation feature enables live validation and revocation; omit
 --features validation for detection only. See the library guide,
 runnable examples, and
 revocation guide.

 Available on crates.io: 
 - kingfisher-scanner
 - kingfisher-rules
 - kingfisher-core

Or install the CLI , scan a codebase, and open the interactive HTML report:

 

Replace /path/to/code with your source directory. Scans validate credentials by
default; add --no-validate for detection only. Add --blast-radius to map supported
credentials' access when authorized. Revocation remains a separate, explicit action.
See the CLI installation guide and
usage guide for more options.

 Scan Targets

Kingfisher handles local files and directories, Git repositories and history, compressed and
office-document archives, SQLite databases, Python bytecode, Docker images, source-hosting
organizations, cloud object storage, collaboration tools, and API-development platforms.

For target-specific commands, authentication, scope, and pagination behavior, use the
platform integration guide.

 Discover, validate, and revoke — open source options

All four tools detect secrets. Kingfisher and Betterleaks 2.0 RC5 also include
credential revocation for supported providers.

 Built-in capability Kingfisher Betterleaks 2.0 RC5 TruffleHog OSS Gitleaks 
 --- :---: :---: :---: :---: 
 (Find) Secret discovery ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ 
 (Validate) Live credential verification ✅ ✅ ✅ ❌ 
 (Revoke) Credential revocation ✅ ✅ ❌ ❌ 
 License Apache-2.0 MIT AGPL-3.0 MIT 

✅ Built in · ❌ Not supported as a built-in capability.

 Built for Speed and Accuracy

Kingfisher's multithreaded Vectorscan engine recorded the lowest runtime on every repository in the published benchmark suite, from small projects through the Linux kernel and GitLab monorepo.
Lower runtimes are better.

 
 
 

See the benchmarks for validation results, network-request counts, and
the test environment, and deployment options for local, CI, and embedded use.

 Why Kingfisher

 Stage What Kingfisher provides Learn more 
 --- --- --- 
 Detect A blazingly fast, multithreaded Vectorscan regex engine combines SIMD-accelerated matching with language-aware verification across repositories, files, archives, cloud storage, containers, and developer platforms Scanning, integrations, benchmarks 
 Validate Live provider checks that distinguish active credentials from static candidates Validation and filtering 
 Map Read-only blast-radius analysis for supported providers, including AWS role and GCP service-account reachability, bounded Bedrock discovery, and Google API-key probes Blast radius 
 Triage A local and hosted browser viewer for filtering, deduplication, prioritization, blast-radius inspection, and export Viewer usage, hosted guide 
 Alert Real-time notifications for findings, with per-sink confidence, validation, and access-map filters Alert webhooks 
 Revoke Conservative provider-specific containment workflows for supported credentials Revocation

install.title: Getting Started
install.html:
Quick Start

Install with your preferred package manager:

# Homebrew (macOS/Linux)
brew install kingfisher

# PyPI wrapper
uv tool install kingfisher-bin

See the full installation guide for all installation methods, installer options, and pre-commit hook installation.

The examples below use Bash syntax. Replace credential placeholders with values from your secret store; local scans need no platform credentials. See the environment-variable reference for other authentication options.

Then scan a repository, including its Git history:

kingfisher scan /path/to/repository --format json

Open the results in the bundled local viewer:

kingfisher scan /path/to/repository --view-report
Scan files and Git history
# Clone a private GitHub repository and scan its Git history (omit the token for public repositories)
KF_GITHUB_TOKEN="..." \
    kingfisher scan https://github.com/my-org/my-repo.git --format json

# Scan checked-out files without Git history or live validation
kingfisher scan /path/to/repository \
    --git-history none \
    --no-validate \
    --format json

# Check staged changes before committing
kingfisher scan . \
    --staged \
    --format json

# Scan an archive or an office document
kingfisher scan backup.tar.gz credentials.xlsx --format json

# Focus on configuration files and skip generated content
kingfisher scan /path/to/repository \
    --path-prefix configs/ \
    --skip-path-prefix configs/generated/ \
    --file-extension env \
    --file-extension yaml \
    --format json

# Show only live credentials and map their access
kingfisher scan /path/to/repository \
    --only-valid \
    --blast-radius \
    --format json

# Include active credentials and high-confidence assumed or locally derived secrets
kingfisher scan /path/to/repository \
    --validation-filter actionable \
    --format json
Save and combine reports
# Save a JSON report and open it later
kingfisher scan /path/to/repository \
    --format json \
    --output findings.json
kingfisher view findings.json

# Export SARIF for code-scanning integrations
kingfisher scan /path/to/repository \
    --format sarif \
    --output findings.sarif

# Generate a standalone HTML audit report
kingfisher scan /path/to/repository \
    --format html \
    --output audit.html

# Import and combine Kingfisher, Gitleaks, and TruffleHog reports
kingfisher view findings.json gitleaks.json trufflehog.jsonl

# Load every supported report in a directory
kingfisher view ./reports/
Scan source-hosting organizations

Use a token with read access to the repositories you want to scan. See the integration guide for provider-specific permissions and self-hosted endpoints.

# GitHub organization
KF_GITHUB_TOKEN="..." \
    kingfisher scan github \
        --organization my-org \
        --format json
# GitHub user and their gist history
KF_GITHUB_TOKEN="..." \
    kingfisher scan github \
        --user alice \
        --include-gists \
        --format json

# GitLab group, including nested subgroups
KF_GITLAB_TOKEN="..." \
    kingfisher scan gitlab \
        --group my-group \
        --include-subgroups \
        --include-snippets \
        --format json

# Azure Repos organization
KF_AZURE_TOKEN="..." \
    kingfisher scan azure \
        --azure-organization my-org \
        --format json

# Bitbucket workspace
KF_BITBUCKET_TOKEN="..." \
    kingfisher scan bitbucket \
        --workspace my-team \
        --include-snippets \
        --format json

# Gitea organization
KF_GITEA_TOKEN="..." KF_GITEA_USERNAME="scanner" \
    kingfisher scan gitea \
        --organization my-org \
        --format json

# Hugging Face organization
KF_HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN="..." \
    kingfisher scan huggingface \
        --huggingface-organization my-org \
        --format json

# Preview the GitHub repository scope without scanning
KF_GITHUB_TOKEN="..." \
    kingfisher scan github \
        --organization my-org \
        --list-only
Scan cloud storage

For S3 and GCS, use a bucket name without s3:// or gs://. Azure Blob uses a full container URL. Use --path-prefix to select object names; S3 and GCS also accept the existing --prefix option. Omit prefix selection to scan the whole bucket or container.

# AWS S3: whole bucket with explicit credentials
KF_AWS_KEY="..." KF_AWS_SECRET="..." \
    kingfisher scan s3 my-bucket --format json

# AWS S3: temporary credentials also require the session token
KF_AWS_KEY="..." KF_AWS_SECRET="..." KF_AWS_SESSION_TOKEN="..." \
    kingfisher scan s3 my-bucket --format json

# AWS S3: only objects under backups/production/, using a named AWS profile
kingfisher scan s3 my-bucket \
    --prefix backups/production/ \
    --profile security \
    --format json

# Google Cloud Storage: whole bucket using a service-account file
GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS="/path/to/service-account.json" \
    kingfisher scan gcs my-bucket --format json

# Google Cloud Storage: only objects under exports/daily/, using existing Application Default Credentials
kingfisher scan gcs my-bucket \
    --prefix exports/daily/ \
    --format json

# Azure Blob Storage: container SAS with read (r) and list (l) permissions
KF_AZURE_STORAGE_SAS="sv=...&sp=rl&sig=..." \
    kingfisher scan azure-blob \
        https://myaccount.blob.core.windows.net/my-container --format json

# Azure Blob Storage: account-key authentication (account name is inferred for standard Azure endpoints)
KF_AZURE_STORAGE_KEY="..." \
    kingfisher scan azure-blob https://myaccount.blob.core.windows.net/my-container --format json

# Azure Blob Storage: an existing Entra access token for https://storage.azure.com/
KF_AZURE_STORAGE_TOKEN="..." \
    kingfisher scan azure-blob https://myaccount.blob.core.windows.net/my-container --format json

# Hugging Face bucket: selected paths with resumable downloads
KF_HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN="..." \
    kingfisher scan huggingface \
        --huggingface-bucket hf://buckets/my-org/data \
        --path-prefix configs/ \
        --object-cache-dir ./object-cache \
        --format json

Authenticate to S3 with KF_AWS_KEY / KF_AWS_SECRET or --profile; GCS uses Application Default Credentials, or an explicit --service-account /path/to/key.json. See the S3 and GCS guides for authentication and public-bucket examples. Azure Blob accepts a container URL; set exactly one of the SAS, account-key, or Entra-token variables, or omit all three for anonymous access to a public container with list/read permissions; see the Azure Blob guide.

Use --path-prefix, --skip-path-prefix, --file-extension, and --skip-file-extension to select paths across local files, Git repositories, archive members, and cloud storage. S3, GCS, Azure Blob, and Hugging Face buckets apply selection before downloading and accept --object-cache-dir to resume interrupted listings and reuse unchanged content. Cached content is rescanned so each report stays complete. Custom HTTP verification services can use OAuth2 password-grant authentication.

Scan containers or run Kingfisher in Docker
# Scan a registry image
kingfisher scan docker ghcr.io/owasp/wrongsecrets/wrongsecrets-master:latest-master --format json

# Pull a private registry image
KF_DOCKER_TOKEN="user:password" \
    kingfisher scan docker ghcr.io/my-org/my-image:latest --format json

# Scan an image exported with docker save
kingfisher scan docker \
    --archive image.tar \
    --format json

# Run Kingfisher against the current directory without installing it
docker run \
    --rm \
    -v "$PWD":/src \
    ghcr.io/mongodb/kingfisher:latest scan /src \
    --format json

# Run in Docker and serve the report viewer to the host
docker run \
    --rm \
    -v "$PWD":/src \
    -p 127.0.0.1:7890:7890 \
    ghcr.io/mongodb/kingfisher:latest scan /src \
    --view-report \
    --view-report-address 0.0.0.0

For the Docker viewer, open localhost:7890 in your browser.

Scan issues, documents, and messages

Jira and Confluence Cloud API tokens require the account email as well as the token. For server bearer tokens, omit KF_JIRA_USER or KF_CONFLUENCE_USER. See the integration guide for required scopes and search behavior.
